blocks.content: J&K's education and health sectors have seen substantial recent institutional expansion, making this a useful current-affairs-adjacent chapter alongside the more historical/constitutional material earlier in the book.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Higher Education Institutions focus on building specialized technical, medical, and academic capabilities.
School Education & Literacy Initiatives aim at universal primary enrollment and foundational literacy.
Health Infrastructure covers primary health centers, rural healthcare schemes, and tertiary medical facilities.
Developing both education and healthcare is essential for boosting human capital and economic productivity.

items: The Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan (the central government's integrated school-education scheme) has been extended to J&K UT alongside various UT-specific initiatives aimed at improving school infrastructure and enrolment, particularly in remote and border areas.

Given J&K's historical literacy gap relative to the national average (Chapter 19), targeted female-literacy and girl-child education initiatives have been a recurring policy emphasis across successive governments.

Government Medical College (GMC) Srinagar and GMC Jammu are the two principal, longest-established government medical colleges of the erstwhile state, supplemented in recent years by several newer medical colleges established across various districts as part of a broader push to expand tertiary healthcare access beyond the two main cities.

Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences (SKIMS), Srinagar, is J&K's premier super-speciality medical institute and research hospital, comparable in role to AIIMS-type institutions elsewhere in India.

Ayushman Bharat (central health-insurance scheme) has been extended to J&K UT, alongside a UT-specific health-insurance scheme in earlier years, aimed at expanding financial protection for healthcare costs across the population.
